question: During the census 2011, which of the following states recorded the lowest growth rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the 2011 Census, Nagaland recorded the lowest population growth rate among Indian states.
 
• The state experienced a negative growth rate of -0.47% between 2001 and 2011.
 
• Nagaland's population decreased from 1,990,036 in 2001 to 1,978,502 in 2011.
 
• This decline is attributed to migration to other states and errors in the previous census enumeration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census in India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first complete census was conducted in 1881, and since then, it has been conducted every ten years.
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on the demographic, social, and economic characteristics of the population.
 
 
 
• **Population Growth Rate**
 
 
• The population growth rate is the rate at which the number of individuals in a population increases in a given time period as a fraction of the initial population.
 
• It is an important indicator of demographic trends and is influenced by factors such as birth rate, death rate, and migration.
 
 
 
• **Migration**
 
 
• Migration refers to the movement of people from one place to another, which can be within a country (internal migration) or between countries (international migration).
 
• Migration can significantly impact the population size and composition of both the origin and destination areas.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Trends**
 
 
• Demographic trends refer to the changes in the population over time, including changes in size, composition, and distribution.
 
• Understanding these trends is crucial for policy-making, planning, and resource allocation.
